chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Muhammad ibn Sinan who said:
I asked him about the name, what is it? He said: It is an attribute for the attributed.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a name in Shia theological discourse?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this concise definition to anchor the discussion on Divine Names (Asma al-Husna) within the broader linguistic and metaphysical framework of 'sifah' (attribute). This establishes that while names are distinct entities, they are fundamentally descriptive qualities inherent to the 'mawsum' (the named), a distinction crucial in Shia theology for understanding how attributes relate to the Essence (Dhat) without becoming separate entities. It serves as a foundational premise before distinguishing between the eternal, essential names of Allah and the contingent, created names of His creation.
